elowen.bio: Elowen Vey grew up among the copyists of a lakeside library, where silence was a virtue and curiosity a vice. Childhood taught her that the careful ones are the ones who come home. She read every treatise on enchanted metal on its shelves until her tutors ran out of answers. On the road she turns back early rather than late, which is exactly why she is still on it. She came south to see arcane metal worked by hand instead of described in margins. When she first set out, she hoped to read the one book no library would lend. She fills the margins of every book she touches, including other people's. What came after she reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

garrick.bio: Garrick Stone was raised by his mother Martha after his father died, and grew up carrying her firewood and her worries. He learned prayers before letters and has never quite stopped saying them. He swore his oath at a wayside shrine and spent two winters guarding pilgrims on the mountain roads. On the road he keeps the old wards and rites, and swears they have saved more lives than steel. He became a paladin to stand between ordinary people and the things that hunt them. When he first set out, he hoped to stand wherever the danger was worst. He mends his own gear and anyone else's who asks. Whatever he has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

kestra.bio: Kestra Dunmore grew up with her brother Tobin in the crowded lanes of a river town, where wit was cheaper than bread. She learned early that nothing is truly lost until someone else has found it. She learned locks and quick exits from the very people she later came to owe money. In a tight corner she still finds a moment to check what the enemy was carrying. She took to adventuring because honest wages would never clear what she owes. When she first set out, she hoped for one great score and a quiet life after it. She never sits with her back to a door. Whatever she has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

mira.bio: Mira Pell grew up above her father Aldric's grocery, counting turnips and customers before she could read. Childhood taught her that the careful ones are the ones who come home. She learned the bow from the herders who traded at the shop door, and the woods from her own wandering. In a tight corner she looks for the way out before the way through. She took up the ranger's road to prove she is more than the grocer's girl. When she first set out, she hoped to walk paths that no map remembers. She still checks the wind before breakfast. Everything since then belongs to the village's own memory.

pip.bio: Pip Underbough grew up behind the bar of a crossroads inn, listening to more travellers' tales than any child should. He learned early that fear is a poor reason to stay at home. He learned the lute from a wandering player who paid for his room in songs. In a tight corner he steps forward first, which has earned him both friends and scars. He set out to collect stories first-hand instead of second-hand over a tankard. When he first set out, he hoped to witness a deed worthy of a ballad. He keeps a notebook of names, tunes and debts owed. What came after he reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

rv_brenna.bio: Brenna Thorn was the only daughter among a pack of brothers on a horse farm in the south. She learned early that patience finishes more work than talent ever starts. She learned to fight in the yard against all of them at once, and to win at least sometimes. In a tight corner she keeps a level head and a level blade. She came north to make a name for herself before her brothers do. When she first set out, she hoped to earn a captain's trust and a captain's pay. She oils every blade at dusk, borrowed or not. What came after she reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

rv_dagny.bio: Dagny Ironvein was raised in a dwarven hall beneath the mountains, where oaths were carved into the doorposts. She learned early that nothing is truly lost until someone else has found it. She kept the old oaths as a hall-warden for longer than most of her companions have been alive. In a tight corner she still finds a moment to check what the enemy was carrying. She left the halls to learn whether the surface world still honours a promise. When she first set out, she hoped to stand wherever the danger was worst. She rises before dawn to keep her vows. Whatever she has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

He learned to fight in the camp's wrestling rings and to roar louder than the drums. In a tight corner he looks for the way out before the way through. He wants to be remembered in a song, preferably a loud one. When he first set out, he hoped for a fight worth retelling by the fire. He eats like two and shares like three. What came after he reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

What came after he reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

tomas.bio: Brother Tomas grew up in a busy market town, raised by a dice-maker who taught him the odds before his prayers. He learned prayers before letters and has never quite stopped saying them. He found his calling in a temple infirmary, where his jokes worked nearly as well as his poultices. In a tight corner he prays aloud, and fights no worse for it. He took to the road as a travelling healer, and the road's card tables took to him. When he first set out, he hoped to bring every companion home alive. He carries more bandages than coin. What came after he reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

varn.bio: Varn Ashfang grew up among the hill clans, where a loud voice and an open hand were counted as wealth. He learned early that the quickest way through trouble is straight through the middle of it. He learned the great axe splitting firewood for a whole winter camp, and broke a good many handles doing it. On the road he strikes first and bandages later, and his scars keep count. He came down from the hills when the old songs stopped being enough for him. When he first set out, he hoped for a fight worth retelling by the fire. He laughs loudest when the odds are worst. Whatever he has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.
